\chapter{Visto que e dado que}

\hlchaptermodality{349}

\section[visto que]{visto que — since, seeing that}

\label{lesson:PT-C349-visto-que}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the factor, then the Portuguese for the consequence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: visto que}
\textbf{visto que} — \textquotedblleft{}since, seeing that\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Visto que está a chover, ficamos em casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Since it is raining, we are staying at home.}
\end{quote}

Takes the indicative. A little formal; in speech \emph{como} at the start of a sentence.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{visto que} is built from \emph{visto} \textquotedblleft{}seen\textquotedblright{}, the participle of \emph{ver}, inherited from Latin \emph{vidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), and \emph{que}, from Latin \emph{quid} (EtymDB): \textquotedblleft{}it being seen that\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{visto que}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{visto que}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{visto que}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the factor, then the Portuguese for the consequence, then say \emph{visto que} again
\end{itemize}

\section[dado que]{dado que — given that}

\label{lesson:PT-C349-dado-que}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the consequence, then the Portuguese for since.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: dado que}
\textbf{dado que} — \textquotedblleft{}given that\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Dado que o comboio está atrasado, vamos chegar tarde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Given that the train is late, we are going to arrive late.}
\end{quote}

Takes the indicative; close to \emph{visto que}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dado que} is built from \emph{dado} \textquotedblleft{}given\textquotedblright{}, the participle of \emph{dar}, inherited from Latin \emph{dare} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), and \emph{que}, from Latin \emph{quid} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dado que}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dado que}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{dado que}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the consequence, then the Portuguese for since, then say \emph{dado que} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[uma vez que]{uma vez que — seeing as, since}

\label{lesson:PT-C349-uma-vez-que}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for since, then the Portuguese for given that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: uma vez que}
\textbf{uma vez que} — \textquotedblleft{}seeing as, since\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Uma vez que já estás aqui, podes ajudar-me.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Since you are already here, you can help me.}
\end{quote}

With the indicative it gives a reason. With the subjunctive it means once or provided that.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{uma vez que} is built from \emph{uma vez} \textquotedblleft{}once\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{vez} inherited from Latin \emph{vicis} \textquotedblleft{}change, turn, place\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), and \emph{que}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uma vez que}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uma vez que}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{uma vez que}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for since, then the Portuguese for given that, then say \emph{uma vez que} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does uma vez que mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Seeing as, since\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[consequentemente]{consequentemente — consequently, as a result}

\label{lesson:PT-C349-consequentemente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for given that, then the Portuguese for seeing as.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: consequentemente}
\textbf{consequentemente} — \textquotedblleft{}consequently, as a result\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Perdi o autocarro e, consequentemente, cheguei atrasado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I missed the bus and, as a result, I arrived late.}
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \emph{por isso}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{consequentemente} is built on \emph{consequente} with the adverb ending \emph{-mente}; \emph{consequente} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{cōnsequēns} \textquotedblleft{}following\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{sequī} \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{consequentemente}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{consequentemente}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{consequentemente}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for given that, then the Portuguese for seeing as, then say \emph{consequentemente} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[devido a]{devido a — due to, because of}

\label{lesson:PT-C349-devido-a}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for seeing as, then the Portuguese for consequently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: devido a}
\textbf{devido a} — \textquotedblleft{}due to, because of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O voo chegou atrasado devido ao nevoeiro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The flight arrived late due to the fog.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Devido a} + noun: \emph{devido à chuva}. With a verb: \emph{devido a ter chovido}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{devido a} is built on \emph{devido} \textquotedblleft{}owed, due\textquotedblright{}, the participle of \emph{dever}, inherited from Latin \emph{dēbēre} \textquotedblleft{}to owe\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): what is owed to a cause.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{devido a}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{devido a}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{devido a}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for seeing as, then the Portuguese for consequently, then say \emph{devido a} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does devido a mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Due to, because of\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
